'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Sixteen people are dead and eight injured after three bombs explode in [[Balad, Somalia|Balad]], [[Mogadishu]] and [[Dinsoor]]. The attacks are claimed by [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]]. The deadliest attack is in Balad, which result in 14 soldiers killed. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/somalia-16-dead-several-injured-in-3-bomb-blasts/2125055 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**The [[European Aviation Safety Agency]] clears the [[Boeing 737 MAX]] passenger [[airliner]] to return to service in [[European Union]] [[airspace]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/eu-regulator-clears-boeing-737-max-for-flights-01611749104?tesla=y (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[GameStop short squeeze]]
**A [[short squeeze]] causes [[GameStop]] [[stock]] to increase tremendously after [[Reddit]] users predicted a [[hedge fund]] closure over the last week. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/jan/27/gamestop-stock-market-retail-wall-street?scrlybrkr=b7d8f0df (''The Guardian'')] [https://apnews.com/article/gamestop-stocks-reddit-surge-039aa5ad00f4b22b4d48a5e5492c4bb5 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Dschang bus-truck crash]]
**A collision between a bus and a truck in [[Dschang]], [[West Region (Cameroon)|West]], [[Cameroon]], kills 53 people and leaves 29 others injured with severe [[burn]]s. [https://mb.com.ph/2021/01/28/53-killed-in-cameroon-bus-blaze/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[Mount Merapi]] on [[Java]], [[Indonesia]], erupts. No casualties have been reported. [https://amp.theguardian.com/world/2021/jan/27/mount-merapi-volcano-erupts-indonesia (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[New Jersey]] confirms their first death from the UK variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in a person who had "significant underlying conditions." [https://patch.com/new-jersey/wayne/first-death-involving-new-covid-variant-case-nj (Patch.com)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alabama]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[Alabama]] confirms their first three cases of the UK variant of SARS-CoV-2 in two children and an adult from [[Montgomery County, Alabama|Montgomery]] and [[Jefferson County, Alabama|Jefferson]] counties. [https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/georgia/articles/2021-01-27/alabama-becomes-latest-state-to-detect-covid-19-variant (U.S. News & World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] reports a record 27,944 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to over 1.8 million. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/mexico-s-new-daily-record-of-almost-28-000-coronavirus-cases-1-623-deaths-121012800158_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] receives his second dose of the [[Sinovac Biotech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/166828/president-jokowi-receives-second-dosage-of-sinovac-covid-19-vaccine (Antara News)]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 387 deaths and 10,974 recoveries in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 28,855 deaths and 831,330 recoveries. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5350697/tambah-11948-kasus-positif-corona-di-ri-27-januari-jadi-1024298?tag_from=wpm_nhl_5 (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Prime Minister]] [[Sheikh Hasina]] launches a [[vaccination]] programme in [[Bangladesh]] using the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine]]. [http://www.newsonair.com/News?title=Prime-Minister-Sheikh-Hasina-launches-COVID-19-vaccination-programme-in-Bangladesh&id=408732 (All India Radio)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****[[Myanmar]] begins a vaccination programme using the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [[Healthcare worker]]s are the first people to be vaccinated. [https://apnews.com/article/aung-san-suu-kyi-myanmar-india-coronavirus-pandemic-asia-e52fa4608d3676d304afd5fd6b8e91c5 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Prime Minister of Nepal|Prime Minister]] [[KP Sharma Oli]] launches a [[vaccination]] campaign against COVID-19 in [[Nepal]] beginning with 430,000 frontline and [[healthcare worker]]s. [https://kathmandupost.com/health/2021/01/27/nepal-launches-its-covid-19-vaccination-drive-starting-with-frontline-and-healthcare-workers (''The Kathmandu Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****[[Cyprus]] announces a cautious easing of the second nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] beginning February 1 following a decline in the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases that peaked after [[Christmas]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210127-cyprus-eases-second-virus-lockdown (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[North Macedonia]] reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in a person with no known travel history who recovered on January 22. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/28/c_139702522.htm (Xinhua)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]]
****[[Prime Minister of Norway|Prime Minister]] [[Erna Solberg]] announces the closure of all borders for non-essential travel beginning January 29 in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|SARS-CoV-2 variant]]s into [[Norway]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidnikel/2021/01/27/norway-closes-border-to-all-but-essential-travel/ (''Forbes'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Prime Minister of Malta|Prime Minister]] [[Robert Abela]] announces the imposition of new measures to stop the curve: restaurants, kiosks, and snack bars must remain closed for the entire month of February from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., bars are completely closed, recommends that schools postpone the two days of school holidays for Carnival. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/watch-live-robert-abela-announces-new-covid-19-measures.847530 (''Times of Malta'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces the introduction of 10-day hotel quarantine for travellers from 30 high-risk countries, including [[Brazil]], Portugal, [[South Africa]], and all [[South America]]n nations due to spread of [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/global-health/science-and-disease/coronavirus-news-covid-deaths-lockdown-end-quarantine-hotels/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****[[Morocco]] receives half a million doses of the [[Sinopharm]] vaccine. [https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2021/01/333436/morocco-receives-half-a-million-doses-of-chinese-sinopharm-vaccine/ (Morocco World News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[South Africa]] approves a [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by the [[University of Oxford]] and [[AstraZeneca]] for emergency use in the country. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/south-africa-approves-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine-for-emergency-use-943987.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
***[[Chile]]'s health regulator approves a [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by the [[University of Oxford]] and [[AstraZeneca]] for emergency use in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-chile-astrazeneca/chile-health-regulator-approves-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine-for-emergency-use-idUSKBN29W1SQ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gretchen Whitmer kidnapping plot]]
**One of the fourteen men accused of [[conspiracy (crime)|conspiring]] to [[kidnap]] [[Michigan]] [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] [[Gretchen Whitmer]] pleads guilty in a [[federal government of the United States|federal]] court and agrees to testify against his co-defendants. His sentencing is scheduled for July 8. [https://www.mlive.com/news/grand-rapids/2021/01/michigan-man-says-he-surveilled-gov-whitmers-home-in-kidnap-plot.html (MLive.com)]
*a 16-year-old far-right extremist boy is arrested in [[Singapore]] for plotting attacks against two mosques on the anniversary of the deadly 2019 [[Christchurch mosque shootings]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/27/singapore-arrests-teenager-for-plotting-attacks-against-muslims (Al Jazeera)]
*In the central Indian state of [[Madhya Pradesh]], 100 [[Hindus|Hindu]] activists attack a prayer gathering in the [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] media center. [https://www.ucanews.com/news/hindu-activists-terrorize-indian-christians-in-catholic-media-center/91173# (UCA News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Statehood movement in the District of Columbia]]
**[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] in the [[United States Senate]] introduce [[DC Admission Act|a bill]] that would make [[Washington, D.C.]] the [[51st state]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/washington-dc-51st-state-bill-senate-democrats/ (CBS News)]
*[[Decommunization in Ukraine]]
**In accordance with [[Ukrainian decommunization laws|decommunization laws]], the last statue of [[Vladimir Lenin]] in the country (excluding territories currently annexed by [[Russia]] or occupied by [[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|separatists]]) is demolished in [[Odesa Oblast]]. [https://www.svoboda.org/a/31072087.html (Svoboda Radio)]
